name: Hackett
why: English sporting-gentleman dress assembled as a wardrobe — tipped polos, crest oxfords, rugby shirts and chinos, with a Savile Row tailoring line above them.
origin: Jeremy Hackett and Ashley Lloyd-Jennings, Portobello Road, 1979 — begun by reselling second-hand English tailoring and rebuilt as a house making it new.
opview: The house presents itself as the keeper of English dress: the clothes a certain Englishman is assumed to already own, made available to everyone else.

onething.n: verified — Jeremy Hackett, asked in an interview to name the one thing, said the logo polo. Heritage is the sub-brand that carries the oversized logo and lettering, so this is that polo. A fetch from here dropped the sub-brand refinement, which the site's scripts likely restore; worth confirming in a browser

notes.prep: the British register rather than the American one, and constitutive rather than referenced — the brand was founded to put this wardrobe back into production
notes.ivy: a cousin of the collegiate canon rather than the canon itself; the oxford and the rugby shirt overlap, the campus lineage does not
notes.craft: a Savile Row address and a made-to-measure and bespoke service sit above the main line at Nº14
notes.cashmere: merino and merino-cashmere carry most of the knitwear
notes.whitet: sells a tee as a basic (price pass); not read for more — seeded 27 Sep 2026, provisional

cities: No US stores. Sixteen UK stores around London including Jermyn Street, 14 Savile Row, Sloane Street and New Bond Street; ships to the US
